correctness.rationale: In this bipartite graph every non-isolated maximal clique is a surviving cross edge, while every mixed maximal stable set is exactly one deleted matching pair. Side stable sets meet every surviving edge, and any isolated singleton clique lies in every maximal stable set, so they create no non-CIS pair. For each deleted pair, exactly (a−1)(b−1)−(t−1) surviving edges avoid its endpoints. Summing over t pairs gives the formula, and the zero/one classifications follow arithmetically. Fresh brute-force enumeration independently generated all maximal cliques and maximal stable sets for all 46 legal triples with 1≤a,b≤4 and matched the formula in every case.

evidence: General structural characterizations can imply some CIS/non-CIS cases for bipartite graphs.
They do not enumerate every disjoint maximal pair for K_(a,b) with a deleted matching.
